title: RADIUS: Split out the illegal Ascend attributes in RFC 6929 space
description:
Ascend products used a large number of RADIUS attributes in an
illegal manner. The subset of attributes in the IETF RFC 6929
extended attribute space are still fairly commonly used, especially
242.

By default we dissect those as the RFC 6929 extended attributes.
We have a preference to disable the RFC 6929 handling.

Including by default a dictionary with the Ascend illegal attributes
in the extended space has no effect when the preference is at its
default value, but causes the Ascend attributes to be used when
the preference is enabled. This makes it easier to use these attributes
by only changing preferences instead uncommenting lines in the
dictionary file.

The AVPs in the lower address space that have been assigned via
IETF Review are much less commonly used these days, and a user would
often not want to use the Ascend illegal values for those even if
using the Ascend AVPs in the extended address space. (The Reserved
for Private Use and Implementation Specific space perhaps are a
third category, but not handled here.)

Fix #15551

@@ -576,6 +576,7 @@ File "${STAGING_DIR}\radius\dictionary.arista"
 File "${STAGING_DIR}\radius\dictionary.aruba"
 File "${STAGING_DIR}\radius\dictionary.ascend"
 File "${STAGING_DIR}\radius\dictionary.ascend.illegal"

 File "${STAGING_DIR}\radius\dictionary.asn"

 File "${STAGING_DIR}\radius\dictionary.avaya"

@@ -676,6 +676,7 @@ File "${STAGING_DIR}\radius\dictionary.arista"
 File "${STAGING_DIR}\radius\dictionary.aruba"
 File "${STAGING_DIR}\radius\dictionary.ascend"
 File "${STAGING_DIR}\radius\dictionary.ascend.illegal"
+File "${STAGING_DIR}\radius\dictionary.ascend.illegal.extended"
 File "${STAGING_DIR}\radius\dictionary.asn"
 File "${STAGING_DIR}\radius\dictionary.audiocodes"
 File "${STAGING_DIR}\radius\dictionary.avaya"

@@ -120,6 +120,16 @@ $INCLUDE dictionary.rfc8559
 #
 $INCLUDE dictionary.iana
 
+#       [wireshark: The following is a subset of the ascend illegal dictionary
+#       with those attributes in the IETF RFC 6929 extended attribute space
+#       (i.e., 241..246). These attributes are still used by some vendors.
+#       Set the preference "Disable Extended Attribute Space (RFC 6929)" to
+#       true to dissect these.
+#       Uncommented because these are ignored unless that preference is changed
+#       from the default. Note the other illegal dictionaries do not use
+#       values in the RFC 6929 space.]
+$INCLUDE dictionary.ascend.illegal.extended
+
 #
 #	These dictionaries define attributes in the IETF managed space.
 #	(i.e. 1..255). This is wrong.  We include them here to allow them.

@@ -0,0 +1,35 @@
+# -*- text -*-
+# Copyright (C) 2019 The FreeRADIUS Server project and contributors
+# This work is licensed under CC-BY version 4.0 https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0
+#
+##############################################################################
+#
+#	Ascend dictionary that illegally uses the RFC space.
+#	Subset in the RFC 6929 extended attribute space.
+#
+##############################################################################
+#
+#	Ascend specific extensions
+#	Used by ASCEND MAX/Pipeline products
+#
+#	This next block is renamed because they share the same
+#	names as the vendor-specific attributes, BUT they occur
+#	in the lower (1-255) RADIUS attribute space.
+#
+#	This subset uses the RFC 6929 extended attribute space (241..246).
+#	Some software still sends these instead of supporting RFC 6929.
+#	Set the preference "Disable Extended Attribute Space (RFC 6929)"
+#	to true in order to dissect these.
+#
+ATTRIBUTE	X-Ascend-Remove-Seconds			241	integer
+ATTRIBUTE	X-Ascend-Data-Filter			242	abinary
+ATTRIBUTE	X-Ascend-Call-Filter			243	abinary
+ATTRIBUTE	X-Ascend-Idle-Limit			244	integer
+ATTRIBUTE	X-Ascend-Preempt-Limit			245	integer
+ATTRIBUTE	X-Ascend-Callback			246	integer
+
+#  VALUEs for X-Ascend-* attributes, copied verbatim from the
+#  VALUEs above, for the VSA versions of Ascend-*.
+#
+VALUE	X-Ascend-Callback		Callback-No		0
+VALUE	X-Ascend-Callback		Callback-Yes		1

@@ -11,6 +11,8 @@
 #	draft-sterman-aaa-sip-00.txt
 #
 #	This is bad... at some point the IETF will allocate these.
+#	[wireshark: These are the experimental values from 00 of the draft RFC,
+#	later registered in RFC 5090 with real values. Comment out?]
 #
 ATTRIBUTE	Digest-Response				206	string
 ATTRIBUTE	Digest-Attributes			207	octets	# stupid format
